samples.summary: 'still ticks a rapid second click on the checkbox itself' dispatches non-cancelable clicks, so the new `preventDefault()` is a no-op and the test cannot exercise the path it claims to cover
samples.evidence: The test builds `new MouseEvent('click', { bubbles: true, detail: 1 })` / `detail: 2` without `cancelable: true` (preview.test.ts:167-168), unlike the sibling tests at :132 and :186 which pass `cancelable: true`. The new code (preview.ts:286) calls `e.preventDefault()` for every checkbox click; on a cancelable event jsdom/browsers revert the checkbox's activation (legacy-canceled-activation), so after the first click the box would be UNCHECKED again and the second click would flip it to checked=true, making `checked` read `true` twice — the very 'untick' the test's comment says must not be swallowed. Because the events are non-cancelable here, the revert never happens and the test passes regardless. It also asserts only `toggles.length === 2`, never the reported `checked` values, so a second toggle reporting the wrong state is invisible. Compare the other tests in the file which use `toEqual([[0, true]])`.

samples.summary: The selection-mapping change in `replacePrefixes` is only tested for the single empty-line caret case; the multi-line and indent/outdent paths it also changes have no selection assertion
samples.evidence: `replacePrefixes` now maps the whole selection with assoc 1, which affects every caller: `toggleKind` (bullet/ordered/task), `shift` → `indentList`/`outdentList`. The only new test is 'puts the caret after the marker when the line was empty' (list-commands.test.ts:40-49), a zero-length caret at offset 0. The function's own docstring claims 'the same lines stay selected' (list-commands.ts:190-191), but with assoc 1 a range whose `from` sits exactly at a line start (which is what `selectLines()` produces at test.ts:24-28) now maps past the newly inserted marker, so the first line is no longer fully selected. No test in list-commands.test.ts asserts `view.state.selection` after a multi-line toggle, after an untoggle (prefix removal), or after indent/outdent — I grepped the file for `selection.main` and it appears only in the two caret tests at :47 and :64.

finding.summary: 'still ticks a rapid second click on the checkbox itself' dispatches non-cancelable clicks, so the new `preventDefault()` is a no-op and the test cannot exercise the path it claims to cover
finding.evidence: The test builds `new MouseEvent('click', { bubbles: true, detail: 1 })` / `detail: 2` without `cancelable: true` (preview.test.ts:167-168), unlike the sibling tests at :132 and :186 which pass `cancelable: true`. The new code (preview.ts:286) calls `e.preventDefault()` for every checkbox click; on a cancelable event jsdom/browsers revert the checkbox's activation (legacy-canceled-activation), so after the first click the box would be UNCHECKED again and the second click would flip it to checked=true, making `checked` read `true` twice — the very 'untick' the test's comment says must not be swallowed. Because the events are non-cancelable here, the revert never happens and the test passes regardless. It also asserts only `toggles.length === 2`, never the reported `checked` values, so a second toggle reporting the wrong state is invisible. verdict.reason: The test's literal text is as quoted (non-cancelable events, only a length assertion), but the alleged defect is not present. The behavior this test claims to cover is the `!onCheckbox &&` exemption in the repeated-click guard at preview.ts:293, which reads only `e.detail` and is entirely independent of cancelability. Tracing the second dispatch: target is the input so `onCheckbox` is true (preview.ts:279), the nested-li guard passes (:297-298), the selection guard is skipped for checkbox clicks (:302), and `data-source-line` is present (:307-309), so the toggle fires (:317). Remove the `!onCheckbox &&` exemption and the second click bails, toggles.length becomes 1, and the assertion at preview.test.ts:169 fails — the test is discriminating, not vacuous, and does not "pass regardless". The `e.preventDefault()` at preview.ts:286 is not the behavior this test names, and it is already covered by cancelable-event tests asserting defaultPrevented === true for both the toggling path (preview.test.ts:132-137) and the refusal path the pre-guard cancellation exists for (preview.test.ts:186-189), plus negative cases at :120-122 and :204-208. The only residual truth — asserting toggles.length instead of the [line, checked] pairs — is a breadth point on a behavior that is genuinely tested, which is minor, not blocking, under this lens's rubric.

finding.summary: Test titled "numbers an ordered list per indent level" uses a fixture with no indent levels, so the per-level counter logic is untested
finding.evidence:
The test at list-commands.test.ts:57-63 mounts `'a
b
c'` — three lines all at indent 0 — and asserts `'1. a
2. b
3. c'`. The behavior it claims to cover is `toggleKind`'s `counters = new Map<number, number>()` keyed by `p.indent.length` (list-commands.ts:222,231-232). With a flat fixture the map only ever has key `0`, so replacing the whole Map with a single `let n = 0` counter would leave this test green. No other test in the file toggles an ordered list over a nested/multi-indent selection (I grepped the file for `toggleOrderedList` — only two uses: this test and none with indentation; the indent/outdent block only uses bullets and a pre-existing `1. a
2. b`). The per-indent-level restart is new behavior shipped with a test that is presented as its coverage but cannot fail on it.

verdict.reason:
Verified in-repo. `toggleKind` numbers ordered items with a per-indent-level counter Map keyed by `p.indent.length` (list-commands.ts:233,242-243), documented as such at list-commands.ts:228, and the effect is observable because `prefixOf` preserves the indent (list-commands.ts:73-77): a nested selection yields `1. a / 1. b / 2. c` per level vs `1. a / 2. b / 3. c` with one counter. The only test naming that behavior, `'numbers an ordered list per indent level'` (list-commands.test.ts:68-74), mounts `'a
b
c'` — all lines at indent 0 — so the map only ever holds key 0 and the asserted `'1. a
2. b
3. c'` is produced identically by a single flat counter; the test cannot fail on the per-level logic. I searched wider than the reviewer for a counterexample: repo-wide grep for `toggleOrderedList` finds only this one test call site plus non-test wiring (editor.ts:582, notes-toolbar.tsx:310); repo-wide grep for `ordered` within packages/notes finds no other test; no e2e/notes tests exist; frontend notes tests (notes-undo-integration.test.ts) do not toggle lists; and the many `'ordered'` hits in packages/docs and packages/slides belong to a separate block-model list implementation (`listKind`/`listLevel`), not this prefix-rewriting code, so docs' nested-level tests cannot cover it. Also checked the indent/outdent describe block (list-commands.test.ts:151-201): it only uses indentList/outdentList, never an ordered toggle over a multi-indent selection. This is in-lane fake coverage (a titled test that cannot fail on the behavior it claims) with no meaningful test elsewhere — major.
